options.text: 28th week of gestation to 28 days after birth

options.label: D
options.text: 22nd week of gestation to 7 days after birth

On examination, the baby is alert and on pinching his skin, it goes back quickly. The infant weighs 5.7 Kg. What is the initial fluid of choice for treating diarrhoea in this infant?

questions.stem: A 3-day-old child is suspected to have an inborn error of metabolism. Further evaluation reveals elevated blood ammonia in the presence of normal blood pH and bicarbonate levels. There are no ketone bodies in the urine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A child is found to have paralysis due to poliovirus infection. Which of the following is false regarding the paralysis seen?

options.label: A
options.text: It is an upper motor neuron type

options.label: C
options.text: Strenuous physical exercise during the onset exaggerates the paralysis

options.label: D
options.text: It can be caused by polio vaccination

questions.stem: A mother brought her 7-year-old child to the OPD because of fever and facial swelling for the past 2 days. She says that he has been refusing to eat because of the pain near the jaw. He has not been vaccinated since birth because of his parent's fear of side effects. On examination, a tender swelling is noted on the jaw as shown in the picture. Which of the following statement is true regarding this patient's diagnosis?

options.label: B
options.text: Salivary gland involvement is limited to the parotids

options.label: C
options.text: Patient is not infectious prior to clinical parotid enlargement

questions.stem: If you were to conduct a death audit on all the cases of under-five paediatric deaths secondary to infective diarrhoea, which of the following pathogens would be responsible for the largest fraction of deaths?

A mother observed unusual redness on the palms of her young child while putting him to sleep. She brings him to your OPD and on examination, you find mild abdominal distension, splenomegaly, and pedal edema. You admit the child for further evaluation, but on the night of admission, he suddenly starts vomiting fresh blood. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
The following image shows the chest X-ray of a preterm neonate who was admitted to the NICU in view of severe respiratory distress. What does this suggest?
questions.stemHtml: The following image shows the chest X-ray of a preterm neonate who was admitted to the NICU in view of severe respiratory distress. What does this suggest?

questions.stem: A mother brought a healthy-looking, 3-month-old infant for routine immunization. As you were giving the shot, you noticed some noisy breathing in the baby, which became worse once he started crying. However, it decreased, as you held him in a prone position. There were no clear signs of distress. According to his mother, he had been feeding well at home and has not had any episodes of apnea or cyanosis. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A junior radiologist performing a fetal doppler follows the direction of the flow of oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus to examine the fetal circulatory vessels. The sequence that he would follow is:

options.label: A
options.text: Umbilical artery → inferior vena cava → ductus venosus → right atrium → left atrium

options.label: B
options.text: Umbilical artery → superior vena cava → right atrium → ductus arteriosus → left atrium

options.label: C
options.text: Umbilical vein → ductus venosus → inferior vena cava → right atrium → left atrium

options.label: D
options.text: Umbilical vein → ductus arteriosus → superior vena cava → right atrium → left atrium

questions.stem: The most common mode of inheritance of congenital heart disease is_____.
You are called to see a cyanotic neonate in the NICU. You note that the neonate has an oxygen saturation of 60%. Which of the following would not be in your differential diagnosis

options.label: B
options.text: Ventricular septal defect with pulmonic stenosis

questions.stem: Hematuria in children is defined as the presence of at least ______ RBCs per high power field in uncentrifuged urine.

A 20-year-old primigravida was rushed to the OT for an emergency caesarean section. Her pregnancy was unplanned and she did not take folic acid supplementation prior to conception. Moreover, owing to the pandemic led lockdown and her remote residence, she could not adhere to regular antenatal care. The newborn was born with a neural tube defect and immediately shifted to the NICU. What is the least likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most common, preventable cause of mental retardation?

Which of the following is the second most common malignancy in childhood?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the clinic because of walking difficulties. His mother says he has always walked on his toes and walks by tilting side-to-side. He also has progressive muscle weakness. There is no history of trauma, fever, or rash. On examination, calf hypertrophy with atrophied thigh muscles is noted as shown below. There is no tenderness on palpation. What is the most probable diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child was brought to the hospital with a history of loose stools. No history of fever or blood in stools. The mother says he is irritable and eagerly drinks water if given. On examination, eyes are sunken and in the skin pinch test, the skin retracted within two seconds but not immediately. What treatment is advised for the child?

options.label: A
options.text: Give oral fluids and zinc supplementation only and ask mother to come back if danger sign develops.

options.label: B
options.text: Give oral fluids and ask mother to continue the same and visit again the next day.

options.label: C
options.text: Consider severe dehydration start IV fluids, IV antibiotics, and refer to higher centre.

options.text: About 20-30% of the infections are symptomatic
